title: JetBrains plugin refuses to connect to a daemon whose /health reports another project
description:
Split from task-e7f4026a (HIGH; a seat adopted another project's daemon through a stale daemon.json). That row's DoD 3 asks for the JetBrains check. Its architect checked the code and found the gap, so this task fixes it, and that row dependsOn this task.

The gap: MoeProjectService.connect() and connectWithRetry() adopt the daemon that .moe/daemon.json names whenever isProcessAlive(pid) && isPortOpen(port). doConnect then opens ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/ws.
- After the project's daemon dies, Windows can reuse its PID, and another project's daemon can take the port.
- The plugin then attaches this window to the other project's board. It registers seats there and sends DEREGISTER_WORKER there (agentSeats.resendGone()).
- Under the PROTECTED profile, activationRefusal (RF01 provenance) already refuses an unrecorded daemon. LEGACY has no check.

Deliverable:
- A small pure helper in a new file, for example moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/DaemonIdentity.kt.
  - It GETs http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health with short connect and read timeouts and a body capped at 64 KiB.
  - It classifies the reply as same, foreign (with the served path) or unknown.
  - It compares paths by the comparable-path rule of packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts comparableProjectPath: D:\x == D:/x == /mnt/d/x, with drive paths case-insensitive.
  - A /mnt/<d> spelling of this project is never foreign: a WSL-hosted daemon serving this project must not be deleted or duplicated.
- MoeProjectService.doConnect, after activationRefusal and before any client is created:
  - A foreign reply is handled like the dead-PID branch.
    - Delete .moe/daemon.json only while it still names the same pid, port and startedAt that were read.
    - Publish a status naming the project that daemon serves, and saying this project's daemon will start on the next free port.
    - Schedule the reconnect, which spawns this project's daemon.
  - An unknown reply proceeds as today.
  - The probe never runs on the EDT.
- JUnit tests:
  - the helper, against a local com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer: same in each spelling, foreign, unreachable, non-JSON, no projectPath, and an oversize body;
  - the doConnect branch, as far as MoeProjectService's test seams allow.

Ordering:
- MoeProjectService.kt is also in CQ-RF04's plan (task-de91373a), which now dependsOn this task.
- Do not edit MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt: RF01, task-0c72d59a, RF03 and RF04 are serialized on it.

Not in scope:
- the proxy and the wrappers (sibling and parent rows);
- VS Code (a BACKLOG follow-up);
- the daemon;
- RF behavior.

implementationPlan.note:
Reopen 1 (QA reject #1, issue 2: header trickle). Added two helper rows to DaemonIdentityTest.kt (+55):
- `trickling headers are cut off by the whole-request deadline and the socket is closed`: a raw ServerSocket sends `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nX-Slow: `, then one header byte every 100 ms for 10 s. probeFast (200/200) must return Unknown in under 2 s, and the responder thread must exit within 3 s, which proves the probe closed its socket and did not abandon a blocked read.
- `the probe never consults the IDE proxy selector`: installs a recording ProxySelector that routes everything to a dead SOCKS proxy. The probe must still classify Foreign, with zero select() calls. This keeps NO_PROXY tested once the transport changes.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red) for the connect branch. New file moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeProjectForeignDaemonTest.kt.

Copy MoeProjectConnectionTest's fixture approach: MoeProjectService(fakeProject, invokeLater = { it() }), and doConnect invoked by reflection with a DaemonInfo. Two differences:
- the fake project's getBasePath returns a temp dir holding .moe/daemon.json {port, pid, startedAt, projectPath: tempDir}. Without .moe/project.json the profile is LEGACY, so activationRefusal is null.
- one com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer on 127.0.0.1:0 serves GET /health with a configurable status and body. It also counts requests on the /ws context: any WebSocket client creation there shows up as an HTTP request.

Capture statuses with service.addListener(object : MoeStateListener { onState {} ; onStatus { add(message) } }). Always call service.dispose() in finally, which cancels the scheduled reconnect, and delete the temp dir.

Rows (the probe runs inline, because the test thread is not the EDT):
- F1, foreign. /health answers {projectPath: <absolute other path>}, and doConnect gets the same pid, port and startedAt as the file.

- S1, same. /health names the temp dir with another spelling (backslashes, or a trailing slash). Within 5 s there is at least one /ws request, and daemon.json is untouched.
- U1, unknown (500, or no projectPath): proceeds exactly as today, with at least one /ws request.

The existing MoeProjectConnectionTest must stay green unedited: its fake project has a null basePath, so the probe is skipped.

implementationPlan.description:
moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeProjectService.kt, doConnect (~:247):

1. Keep the guard and activationRefusal exactly as they are. Then set `connecting = true`, as today.
2. Move the existing client creation, from the wsLock client swap through newClient.connect() and its catch, unchanged into `private fun openClient(daemonInfo: DaemonInfo)`.
3. Add `private fun probeThenOpen(daemonInfo: DaemonInfo)`:
   - The identity is Unknown when project.basePath is null or blank, else DaemonIdentityProbe.probe(daemonInfo.port, basePath).
   - If `disposed.get()` is set, set connecting = false and return.
   - Foreign: call handleForeignDaemon.
   - Otherwise: call openClient(daemonInfo).
4. Never probe on the EDT. If `SwingUtilities.isEventDispatchThread()`, run `scheduler.execute { probeThenOpen(daemonInfo) }`, catching RejectedExecutionException into connecting = false. Otherwise call probeThenOpen inline. projectOpened can call connect() on the EDT.
5. handleForeignDaemon(daemonInfo, foreign, basePath):
   - Re-read the file with daemonSupervisor.readDaemonInfo(). Delete <basePath>/.moe/daemon.json ONLY when it still has the same pid, port and startedAt as daemonInfo. Log the result either way, and catch IO errors.
   - log.warn the event.
   - Set connecting = false BEFORE the next two calls, because scheduleReconnect returns early while connecting.
   - publishStatus(false, "Daemon on port <port> serves another project (<foreign.projectPath>); this project's daemon will start on the next free port.")
   - scheduleReconnect(). This mirrors connect()'s dead-PID branch: the next connect() finds no daemon.json, and ensureDaemonRunning spawns this project's daemon.

MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt is NOT edited: RF01, task-0c72d59a, RF03 and RF04 are serialized on it. Use only its existing readDaemonInfo.

Error handling:
- the probe never throws;
- a delete failure is logged and the reconnect still runs;
- unknown always proceeds as today.

Run both new test files until they are green.

comments.author: architect-bd1eb82d
comments.content: Planner note (architect-bd1eb82d): the daemon's /health reports `projectPath` as the raw --project argument (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts, around line 61), so it can be relative. Classify a relative served projectPath as 'unknown' and proceed as today; never call it 'foreign'. Only an absolute path (drive-letter, UNC or POSIX) that differs by the comparable-path rule counts as foreign, and deleting daemon.json on a false 'foreign' would orphan a live daemon. A 503 'unhealthy' reply that carries an absolute, different projectPath is still foreign. Add helper test rows for both.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Under every profile, after activationRefusal, doConnect probes http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health off the EDT before creating any WebSocket client. A reply naming another project (200 or 503, absolute projectPath, different by the comparable-path rule) gets no client and no seat traffic. daemon.json is deleted only if it still names the same pid, port and startedAt, a status names the other project, and the reconnect spawns this project's daemon. A same or unknown reply proceeds exactly as today.
acceptanceCriteria: F1: a foreign daemon gets zero /ws requests, wsClient null, daemon.json deleted, a status naming the other project, and a scheduled reconnect.
F2: a changed daemon.json (a different startedAt) is kept.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Probe /health in doConnect, after activationRefusal and before any client exists (chosen, as the task specifies). doConnect is the single entry for connect() and connectWithRetry().
- Probing inside connect() before doConnect: rejected, because it would miss connectWithRetry and duplicate the logic.
- Editing MoeDaemonSupervisor (readDaemonInfo or isPortOpen): forbidden. Four rows are serialized on that file.
- Treating a relative or 503 reply per the planner note: relative is Unknown and 503-foreign is Foreign. The same rule was amended into the proxy sibling, task-86093c3e.
- \\wsl$ / \\wsl.localhost project paths: the comparable rule maps them to their POSIX tail, so a WSL-hosted daemon serving this project is never Foreign. That errs toward Same, because a false Foreign deletes daemon.json and spawns a duplicate daemon.

issues.description: DoD 1/F2: readDaemonInfo deletes a rewritten file on projectPath mismatch BEFORE the pid/port/startedAt guard. Repro S1 -> pid=5252/S2/foreign path loses the new file. Use a bounded, side-effect-free reread; delete only after all identity fields match. Keep supervisor unchanged; seek a plan amendment if necessary. Add changed-identity regressions with foreign and equivalent WSL projectPath, asserting exact replacement bytes survive. The follow-up does not defer this requirement.

Contract invariant 1: responseCode reads headers before the deadline check. Header bytes every 100ms defeat a 200ms inactivity timeout: QA measured 3026ms despite 200ms connect/read limits; endless trickling stalls the scheduler. Enforce a whole-request deadline including headers/status/body, abort the underlying request without leaking blocked threads, and return Unknown on expiry.
